title: The Time When the Network Becomes Idle
summary: A network consists of n servers labeled from 0 to n-1, where server 0 is the master server and the rest are data servers.
statement: A network consists of n servers labeled from 0 to n-1, where server 0 is the master server and the rest are data servers. Each data server sends a message to the master server for processing and waits for a reply. Messages travel along the shortest path, and a data server i resends its message every patience[i] seconds if it has not yet received a reply. The network is considered idle when no messages are being sent or received. The earliest second at which the network becomes idle is to be determined.
constraints: edges forms a connected undirected network rooted at master server zero.
A server’s message reply returns after twice its shortest-path distance; it resends every patience seconds before that reply.
Return the first second after every reply has arrived and no message is traveling.
hints: Shortest-path distance determines each message’s fixed round-trip time.
BFS from server zero, then compute the final resend strictly before each first reply.
BFS gives minimum travel time, integer division identifies the greatest resend multiple below the reply, and the network becomes idle one second after the latest arrival time.
editorial: BFS gives minimum travel time, integer division identifies the greatest resend multiple below the reply, and the network becomes idle one second after the latest arrival time.

tests.explanation: Server two last resends at second three and its four-second round trip returns at seven, so the network is idle at eight.
The only reply arrives at second two, making second three the first idle time.
